The task: "In what year did Hjalmar Hvam invent a mechanism that allowed skiing athletes to release the binding that secured their shoes to the boards in case of an emergency after his first injury?" So they ask for the year of invention after his first injury.

The response: The final answer says: "Hjalmar Hvam invented the safety ski binding mechanism (known as the "Saf-Ski") in 1937, immediately following his first injury that same year when he broke his leg while skiing near Timberline Lodge on Mount Hood. He conceived of the design while recovering in the hospital, and the binding was later introduced to the public in 1939-1940."

Thus they claim invention year 1937.

Now we need to see if any tool evidence contradicts that. Let's examine tool responses:

Step 2 web_search result: "Hjalmar Petterson Hvam (November 16, 1902 – March 30, 1996) was a Norwegian-American Nordic skier and the inventor of the world's first workable safety ski binding. Born in Kongsberg, Norway, he began skiing at an early age and achieved success in local competitions. After suffering a leg injury in 1937, he developed a ski binding that would release during a fall, significantly improving safety in the sport. His invention, known as the "Saf-Ski" binding, was introduced in 1939."

So that says: after suffering a leg injury in 1937, he developed a ski binding... His invention, known as the "Saf-Ski" binding, was introduced in 1939.
